brief:
Idea: Show the pair at the end of a hospital night shift, not fresh from the box, because comfort is only proven after the hours are worked.
Headline: Still comfortable at clocking off
Supporting line: A cushioned insole and a grippy sole made for people who stand on hard floors all shift.
Picture: A nurse on an empty ward corridor at the end of a shift, sitting on a bench, one foot slipped half out of {product} to show the insole, the other still laced.
Caption idea: Ask readers who stands longest at their work, name the sole and insole materials from {materials}, and point to sizes at {link}.
mechanism: Comfort claims land when the shoe is shown after a full working day, because that is the moment buyers fear blisters.
expect: A real worker at shift end with the insole visible, no studio pose.

brief:
Idea: Remove the biggest fear of buying shoes online, the wrong size, by teaching a two-minute home measure that matches our chart.
Cover: Get your size right first time
Slides: Slide 2: Stand on paper — heel against the wall, mark the tip of your longest toe.
Slide 3: Measure heel to mark — then find that length on our chart at {link}.
Slide 4: How {product} fits — {fit_note}, so you know whether to size up.
Slide 5: Between two sizes — pick the one {between_sizes_advice} suggests for this pair.
Last slide: Still wrong? {exchange_policy}, no forms to print.
Caption: Save this before you order; it works for every pair we sell.
mechanism: A size method buyers can do at home, plus a clear exchange rule, removes the main reason people abandon a shoe order.
expect: A practical measuring guide with real feet and paper, ending on the exchange rule.

brief:
Offer: {offer} on hand-stitched khussa for the whole family, delivered before Eid when ordered by {date}.
For: Families in Pakistan and the diaspora who buy new shoes for Eid morning.
Angle: New shoes are part of the Eid ritual; ordering late means walking to prayer in last year's pair.
Headline: New khussa for Eid morning
Supporting line: Sizes for parents and children, packed in one box and at your door before chaand raat.
Picture: A row of shoes left outside a mosque door after Eid prayer, one new embroidered pair standing out among the worn ones.
Button: Order before Eid
mechanism: Eid shoes are bought against a hard deadline, so a stated order-by date turns browsing into a purchase this week.
expect: The mosque-doorstep row of shoes with the new pair, deadline in the copy.

brief:
Idea: Launch {product}, a road running shoe, on the run it was built for: wet city streets before work, not a treadmill set.
Shots: Shot 1 (0–1s): A runner's foot lands in a puddle on an empty city pavement, water flicks up.
Shot 2 (1–3s): Laces pulled tight on a park bench, breath visible in the cold air.
Shot 3 (3–5s): The shoe flipped over in a hand, a thumb running along the outsole grooves.
Shot 4 (5–7s): The runner takes a wet corner without slowing, feet steady on the paving stones.
Shot 5 (7–9s): The muddy pair on a doorstep with the name {product} and Out {date}.
Sound: Real footsteps, rain and breathing, one low beat as the name lands.
Caption idea: Say which runs it is made for, using {product_use}, the launch date {date} and the preorder link {link}.
mechanism: Grip is believed when the shoe is seen on the slippery ground runners actually face, not on a clean studio floor.
expect: A short launch film on wet streets with the outsole shown and the date at the end.

brief:
Idea: A shoe that can be resoled outlives trends; show the stitched welt that makes a second life possible.
Headline: Made to be resoled
Supporting line: The sole is stitched, not glued, so a cobbler replaces the sole instead of you replacing the shoes.
Picture: A cobbler's bench with {product} upside down, the worn sole half pulled away, the welt stitching visible and a fresh sole waiting beside it.
Caption idea: Explain in two sentences what a welt is, say where to get them resoled ({resole_service}), and link {link}.
mechanism: Showing how a shoe is repaired answers the doubt that soles wear out, and justifies a higher price as cost over years.
expect: A real cobbler's bench with the welt and both soles in view.

brief:
Idea: Parents in South Africa buy school shoes in January and dread scuffed toes by February; show the toe cap built for break-time football.
Frame 1: Built for break-time football
Middle frames: A child's school shoe mid-kick at a tennis ball on a school yard; a parent's thumb pressing the reinforced toe cap; the size chart beside a traced foot; a poll asking how many pairs they bought last year.
Last frame: {product}, sizes {size_range}, {price}. Order by {date} at {link} for the first school day.
mechanism: School-shoe buyers judge durability by the toe, so showing where kids scuff it most speaks to the parent's real worry.
expect: A child kicking a ball in school shoes, the toe cap and the order-by date.

brief:
Idea: People cannot smell a screen, so translate {product} into the real things it smells of, one layer at a time, as the perfumer wrote it.
Cover: What you will smell, hour by hour
Slides: Slide 2: First spray — {top_notes}, shown as the real peel, leaf or spice on a dresser.
Slide 3: After the first hour — {heart_notes}, the part people ask you about.
Slide 4: By evening — {base_notes}, what stays on your scarf the next day.
Slide 5: Wear it to — {occasions}, the moments it was blended for.
Last slide: {product}, {concentration}, {price}. Order at {link}.
Caption: Tell us which note you noticed first; the full pyramid is on {link}.
mechanism: Naming notes as real objects lets a buyer imagine a smell they cannot test, which lowers the fear of a blind buy.
expect: Each slide shows the actual ingredients of a note layer, ending on the bottle and price.

brief:
Offer: Alcohol-free attar {product} for Ramadan nights, {offer} when ordered before {date}.
For: Men and women in the Gulf and South Asia who wear attar to taraweeh and on Eid morning.
Angle: Many prefer an alcohol-free oil for prayer, and a few drops on the wrist carry through the night prayers.
Headline: For the nights of Ramadan
Supporting line: A rollerball attar of {notes}, made without alcohol, small enough for a thobe or kurta pocket.
Picture: A prayer mat rolled beside a pair of slippers, a small attar bottle and a folded prayer cap on a wooden shelf by the door.
Button: Shop attar
mechanism: For prayer, being alcohol-free is the deciding fact for many buyers, so stating it first removes the reason not to buy.
expect: Ramadan routine objects with the attar, alcohol-free stated plainly.

brief:
Offer: A discovery set of {sample_count_words} samples for {sample_price}, with the full cost taken off your first full bottle.
For: People who have wasted money on a perfume that smelled nothing like its description.
Angle: Wear each sample for a whole day before deciding; the set pays for itself when you choose.
Headline: Wear it before you buy
Supporting line: A week of testing on your own skin, then {sample_price} back on the bottle you pick.
Picture: A row of small labelled vials in a slim box on a work desk, one open beside a notebook with a hand-written note against each scent.
Button: Get the set
mechanism: A paid sample that is credited back removes the blind-buy risk without giving product away free.
expect: Sample vials in daily use with the credit-back offer clear.

brief:
Idea: In India, Diwali visits mean arriving with a gift; show {product}'s gift box handed over at a relative's door and opened on the spot.
Shots: Shot 1 (0–2s): A family on a doorstep with diyas along the step, a young man holding the wrapped box.
Shot 2 (2–4s): An aunt unties the ribbon, lifts the lid, the bottle inside its box.
Shot 3 (4–5s): She sprays it once on her wrist and holds it out for her husband to smell.
Shot 4 (5–7s): Everyone leans in, laughing; a child asks for a spray too.
Shot 5 (7–9s): The box on a sweets tray with {product}, {price} and Order by {date}.
Sound: Doorbell, firecrackers far away, chatter, then the spray.
Caption idea: Suggest it as the gift for the hosts you visit this Diwali, state the notes {notes} and the last order date {date}.
mechanism: Showing the gift being opened by the person it is for helps buyers picture giving it, which is the job a festive gift does.
expect: A real Diwali doorstep exchange, the spray shared, gift box and date at the end.

brief:
Idea: Launch {product}, an evening scent made for long Lagos owambe parties, where you dance for hours in aso ebi and still want to smell good at the end.
Frame 1: Made for the owambe
Middle frames: A woman in aso ebi spraying before leaving the house; the party in full swing, dancing under the canopy; a friend leaning close at the end of the night to ask what she is wearing; a quiz sticker asking which note they guess first.
Last frame: {product} lands {date}. Notes: {notes}. Turn on reminders at {link}.
mechanism: Tying a scent to a specific occasion buyers already dress up for tells them when to wear it, which is half the purchase decision.
expect: A launch story anchored in a real owambe night, with the launch date.

brief:
Idea: Most people spray perfume into the air and walk through it; show where it really lasts, so the scent they bought works the way it should.
Headline: Spray here, not the air
Supporting line: Pulse points and fabric hold scent longest; your hair and scarf carry it all day.
Picture: A person mid-routine before work, spraying the inside of a wrist, the bottle of {product} on the shelf and a scarf ready on the hook.
Caption idea: List four places to apply and two to avoid, explain that rubbing wrists breaks the top notes, and point to {link} for the full notes.
mechanism: Teaching buyers how to apply scent fixes the most common reason they think a perfume fades, so the product gets a fair chance.
expect: A helpful how-to post with the real bottle and a real routine moment.

brief:
Idea: In small flats in Hong Kong and Singapore the sofa question is not style but will it get through the lift and door; answer that first.
Cover: It will fit through your door
Slides: Slide 2: Arrives in parts — back, seat and arms come in separate boxes.
Slide 3: Measure three things — lift door, flat door, tightest corner of the hall.
Slide 4: The biggest box — {box_size}, smaller than most lift doors.
Slide 5: Built in your room — our team bolts it together in {assembly_time}.
Last slide: {product}, {price}, delivered and assembled in {area}. Order at {link}.
Caption: Send us your door measurements and we will tell you before you pay.
mechanism: In small homes the fear is that a sofa will not get in, so showing how it arrives beats showing how it looks.
expect: Practical slides of boxes, doors and assembly, ending on price and area.

brief:
Idea: In our Chiniot workshop, every drawer is joined by hand; show one dovetail joint being cut and fitted, the detail that keeps a dresser square for decades.
Shots: Shot 1 (0–2s): A carpenter marks a line on a drawer side with a pencil and square.
Shot 2 (2–4s): Saw strokes, wood chips falling on the bench.
Shot 3 (4–6s): A chisel clears the waste between the pins.
Shot 4 (6–8s): The two parts tapped together with a mallet, a perfect fit.
Shot 5 (8–9s): The finished dresser in a family bedroom, drawer sliding shut, {product} and {link}.
Sound: Saw, chisel and mallet, no music until the last second.
Caption idea: Name the wood {wood_type}, explain why a dovetail outlasts glue and staples, and show where to order.
mechanism: Watching a joint being cut by hand answers the doubt about whether wood furniture is solid, before price is even raised.
expect: Real workshop hands cutting and fitting a joint, then the piece at home.

brief:
Idea: Eid lunch is when the whole family comes and the table is never long enough; show the extending table that seats everyone, opened in a real home.
Headline: One more leaf for Eid
Supporting line: {product} opens from four seats to {extended_seats} in seconds and closes again when the guests go.
Picture: A dining room in Riyadh on Eid afternoon, the extended table full of dishes, cousins on mismatched chairs, an aunt passing rice across.
Caption idea: Ask how many usually sit at their Eid table, give closed and open lengths {dimensions}, delivery before {date} in {area}.
mechanism: Furniture sells around hosting moments, because a gathering shows the exact problem the piece solves.
expect: A crowded Eid table in a real home with the extension in use.

brief:
Offer: Launch of {product}, a shelving system that stands without drilling, {offer} in the launch week.
For: Renters in Berlin who move every few years and lose their deposit to wall holes.
Angle: Furniture you take with you; it leans and locks, so the wall stays as the landlord left it.
Headline: No holes, full deposit
Supporting line: Tension posts from floor to ceiling, assembled with one key, packed flat when you move.
Picture: A renter in a half-packed flat, the shelving folded flat beside moving boxes, the bare wall behind it with no marks.
Button: See the shelves
mechanism: Renters avoid buying storage they cannot take with them; naming the deposit makes the hidden cost of drilling visible.
expect: A moving-day scene with the shelving flat-packed and an unmarked wall.

brief:
Idea: Fabric never looks the same on a screen; invite people in Toronto to order free swatches and hold them against their own room before choosing.
Frame 1: Hold it against your wall
Middle frames: A swatch box arriving on a doormat; hands spreading the swatches on a sofa arm; each swatch laid beside a cushion, a rug and the curtains; a poll asking which one they would pick.
Last frame: {swatch_count_words} swatches, free to {area}. Request yours at {link}.
mechanism: Seeing fabric in the buyer's own room removes the doubt that it will not match, and a swatch request names a warm lead.
expect: A swatch box being opened and tested in a real living room.

brief:
Idea: Our pieces in customers' own homes, shared with their permission, show what no showroom can: how the sofa looks with real children, real books and real clutter.
Headline: In {customer_first_name}'s living room
Supporting line: {product} in a Nairobi flat, a year into family life.
Picture: The customer's own photo of {product} in their lounge, a child's school bag on one end, a stack of books on the arm, shared with permission.
Caption idea: Quote {review_quote} as given, name the fabric and size, and invite other customers to share their rooms with {hashtag}.
mechanism: A customer's own room is proof that the piece looks good outside a showroom, which is the doubt most furniture buyers carry.
expect: A real customer room photo, credited, lived-in and uncleaned.

brief:
Idea: Launch day for {game_title}: open on the single most surprising moment of real gameplay, so a scroller knows the genre and the hook in one second.
Shots: Shot 1 (0–2s): {hook_moment}, captured straight from the game, no menus on screen.
Shot 2 (2–4s): The core mechanic {mechanic} in two hard cuts.
Shot 3 (4–6s): The world opens up, the player character seen small against it.
Shot 4 (6–7s): One unexpected beat: {twist_moment}.
Shot 5 (7–9s): Logo lockup, Out now on {platforms}.
Sound: The game's own soundtrack, cut on the hits, ending on one in-game sound effect.
Caption idea: Out now on {platforms}; one line on what the player does, and {link} to buy.
mechanism: Players decide in the first second whether a game is for them, so leading with real gameplay beats leading with a logo.
expect: Real gameplay first, mechanic clear, logo and platforms last.

brief:
Offer: A free demo of {game_title}, playable during the online demo festival from {date}.
For: Players of {genre} games who try demos before they wishlist.
Angle: The demo is the first {demo_length_words} of the real game, saves carry over at launch.
Headline: Play the first chapter free
Supporting line: Your save carries into the full game when it launches on {release_date}.
Picture: A real gameplay capture from the demo's most striking moment, the logo lockup and the demo dates in one corner.
Button: Play the demo
mechanism: A demo with a carried-over save turns a free taster into an early commitment to buy the full game.
expect: An ad built on a real demo moment with dates and the save carry-over.

brief:
Idea: Players worry an indie game will never ship; show the same level from our first build and from today, so they can see the work is real.
Cover: Same level, one year apart
Slides: Slide 2: The first build — blank boxes and a placeholder hero.
Slide 3: Six months later — the art pass lands; {change_one}.
Slide 4: Today — {change_two}, after what playtesters told us.
Slide 5: What is left — {remaining_work}, and our plan to finish it.
Last slide: {game_title}, coming {release_date} to {platforms}. Wishlist at {link}.
Caption: Tell us which change you noticed first; the next devlog is out {date}.
mechanism: A then-and-now of the studio's own builds is proof of progress, which answers the fear that a game will not ship.
expect: Real build screenshots, the same level, honest about what is left.

brief:
Idea: Meet the person behind the sound: our audio lead makes the {creature} roar with {sound_object}, a story that makes players listen more closely.
Headline: That roar is {sound_object}
Supporting line: {team_member_name} records every sound in {game_title} from real objects in our studio.
Picture: The audio lead at a desk with a microphone pointed at {sound_object}, headphones on, the game's level paused on the monitor behind.
Caption idea: Tell the story of finding the sound, invite players to guess another one, and link the wishlist {link}.
mechanism: Showing the people and odd craft behind a game gives players a reason to care before they have played it.
expect: A real team member recording foley with a surprising object.

brief:
Idea: For Lunar New Year, players in East Asia log in to see the town in {game_title} dressed for the festival, with lanterns and a limited event.
Frame 1: The town is celebrating tonight
Middle frames: The square in-game hung with lanterns; a character handing out lucky-money envelopes as an event reward; the event's one new mechanic, {event_mechanic}; a countdown sticker to the event's end.
Last frame: Event live {date} to {end_date}. Update now on {platforms}.
mechanism: A seasonal in-game event gives lapsed players a dated reason to return, and a countdown makes the reason urgent.
expect: Real in-game event screens and the dates of the event.

brief:
Offer: Join the closed playtest of {game_title} before launch, sign up by {date}.
For: Players in Brazil and Latin America who want to shape a {genre} game while it can still change.
Angle: We read every report; the bugs you find are the ones nobody meets at launch.
Headline: Break our game first
Supporting line: Playtest from {date}, report through our form, see your fix in the patch notes.
Picture: A gameplay capture of a deliberately funny bug from an old build, a character stuck halfway into a wall, labelled Fixed thanks to a playtester.
Button: Join the playtest
mechanism: Inviting players to find bugs turns doubt about quality into participation, and a sign-up is the earliest buying signal.
expect: A real old bug capture with a playtest sign-up and date.

brief:
Idea: For Mother's Day in Mexico, show the maker embroidering a mother's name onto a cotton napkin, stitch by stitch, so the gift is visibly made for one person.
Shots: Shot 1 (0–2s): The maker's hands pull thread through a hoop, the first letter of {sample_name} forming.
Shot 2 (2–4s): Flowers stitched around the name, sped up.
Shot 3 (4–6s): The napkin folded and tied with ribbon around a small card.
Shot 4 (6–8s): A daughter places it at her mother's plate at breakfast; the mother traces the name.
Shot 5 (8–9s): Name your gift by {date}, {price}, {link}.
Sound: Thread through fabric, then breakfast table chatter.
Caption idea: Explain how to send the name and the order-by date for Mother's Day delivery in {area}.
mechanism: A name being stitched shows the gift is made for one person, which is what makes a handmade gift worth the wait.
expect: Maker's hands embroidering a name, then the mother receiving it.

brief:
Offer: Hand-painted ceramic ornaments with a name and year painted on, order by {date} to have them for the tree.
For: Families in the UK starting or keeping a tradition of one new ornament each Christmas.
Angle: The last order date is real because each one is painted and fired by hand; late orders arrive in January.
Headline: Their name, on the tree
Supporting line: Each ornament painted by our maker with the name you send, fired and boxed for posting.
Picture: A child's hand hanging a ceramic ornament with their name on a tree branch, older named ornaments from past years hanging around it.
Button: Add a name
mechanism: Handmade gifts sell on a firm order-by date, because the buyer's worry is not the price but missing the day.
expect: A named ornament on a real tree with the order-by date in the headline.

brief:
Idea: Meet the Kashmiri papier-mâché artisan behind every box we sell, so buyers see the days of handwork behind a small gift and why it costs what it does.
Cover: One box, many days of hands
Slides: Slide 2: Paper soaked to pulp — {maker_name} presses it over a mould by hand.
Slide 3: Dried and smoothed — layers rubbed with a stone until even.
Slide 4: Painted freehand — the motif drawn with a fine brush, no stencil.
Slide 5: Varnished and signed — each box carries the maker's initials.
Last slide: Boxes from {price}, made to order in {lead_time}. Order at {link}.
Caption: Share {maker_name}'s story as they told it, with their permission.
mechanism: Showing each step of the handwork explains the price of a craft piece and separates it from factory goods called handmade.
expect: A process carousel with a named maker, from pulp to signed box.

brief:
Idea: Companies in India buy Diwali gifts for whole teams and dread late, identical hampers; invite HR and office managers to enquire early for handmade sets with each name.
Frame 1: Diwali gifts for your whole team
Middle frames: A table of hampers being packed by our team, each with a hand-written name tag; a close look at the brass diya and handmade candle inside; a question sticker asking how many people are on their list.
Last frame: Bulk orders by {date}, delivered to your office in {area}. Send your list at {link}.
mechanism: Corporate buyers fear late or generic gifts, so a clear order deadline and named tags turn a busy task into an easy enquiry.
expect: Hampers being packed with name tags and a clear bulk deadline.

brief:
Idea: Answer the fear that a handmade mug will not look like the photo by saying it plainly: yours will be a sibling of this one, never a twin.
Headline: A sibling, never a twin
Supporting line: Every mug is thrown and glazed by hand, so the drips and shape vary a little on each one.
Picture: Five mugs from the same batch in a row on the potter's bench, the small differences in handle and glaze drips easy to see.
Caption idea: Explain why no two match, show {maker_name} at the wheel in the second image, and say how long a mug takes to make: {lead_time}.
mechanism: Showing variation upfront turns the main complaint about handmade goods into the proof that they are handmade.
expect: A batch of slightly different mugs side by side on a real bench.

brief:
Idea: At the weekend craft market in Accra, people can meet our kente weavers and watch a strip woven on the loom before they buy.
Headline: Watch the loom this Saturday
Supporting line: Our weavers at {venue} on {date}, with stoles, bags and gifts woven in front of you.
Picture: A weaver at a narrow strip loom at a market stall, a finished kente stole hanging on the frame behind and visitors leaning in to watch.
Caption idea: Give the stall location {venue}, the hours {hours}, and invite people to bring a name for a woven bookmark made on the spot.
mechanism: A live demonstration at a market gives people a reason to visit the stall, and seeing the craft made justifies buying in person.
expect: A weaver at work at a market stall with date and place.

brief:
Idea: Shoppers compare prices before they leave the house; publish this week's real prices for the staples people buy every week, so the trip is decided at home.
Cover: This week's prices, no small print

Slide 3: Dairy — milk, eggs, yoghurt at {dairy_prices}.
Slide 4: Pantry — rice, flour, oil at {pantry_prices}.
Slide 5: This week only — {weekly_offer}, while stock lasts.

Caption: Prices valid until {date}; ask us at the till if any shelf tag disagrees.
mechanism: A plain weekly price list answers the doubt that the store is dearer than the shop next door before the shopper sets out.
expect: Real shelf prices by category, ending on hours and address.

brief:
Offer: Ready-packed Ramadan ration bags of {bag_contents} for {price}, delivered to a family in need through {charity_partner}.
For: Customers in Karachi who give rations every Ramadan but have no time to shop and pack them.
Angle: Pay at the till or online, we pack and deliver; you get the delivery note for your records.
Headline: Your ration bag, delivered

Button: Sponsor a bag
mechanism: Making a seasonal charity habit easy turns the store into the way people give, without competing on price.
expect: Real staff packing ration bags with contents and partner named.

brief:
Idea: Show that our produce really is fresh by filming today's delivery from the wholesale market being unloaded and on the shelves before we open.
Shots: Shot 1 (0–2s): The van doors open in the early morning, crates of tomatoes and spinach inside.
Shot 2 (2–4s): A staff member wheels the crates through the back door.
Shot 3 (4–6s): Hands stacking tomatoes on the display, the price tag slotted in.
Shot 4 (6–8s): The shutter rolls up, the first customer walks in.
Shot 5 (8–9s): Today's arrivals: {arrivals}. Open from {hours}.
Sound: Van doors, crates, shutter, then the store's own bell.
Caption idea: Name what came in today, where it came from ({source}), and remind people the store opens at {hours}.

brief:
Idea: Busy families in Dubai want groceries tonight without the drive; make the cut-off time the whole message.

expect: A story following one order from message to doorstep with the cut-off.

brief:
Idea: For Lunar New Year in Toronto, families shop for the reunion dinner in one trip; show the shelf where everything on that list sits together.
Headline: Your reunion dinner, one aisle
Supporting line: Whole fish, dumpling wrappers, glutinous rice, mandarins and lucky-money envelopes, stocked together until {date}.

mechanism: Gathering a festival's shopping list in one place saves the shopper the hunt, which is the real reason to choose one store.
expect: A real festival aisle with a family shopping from a list.

brief:
Idea: When the first Sindhri mangoes of summer arrive in Hyderabad, invite neighbours to taste before they buy a whole crate.

Supporting line: Free tasting at the front of the store, {date}, from {hours}; crates at {price}.

brief:
Idea: Muslim families in Birmingham want to know their meat is halal and fresh; introduce the butcher counter, the butcher and how the meat reaches it.

Slides: Slide 2: {butcher_name} — at our counter for {years}, ask for any cut.

Slide 4: Delivered how often — {delivery_days}, cut fresh at the counter.

brief:
Idea: Most people never book a first class because they do not know what happens inside; walk them through the first visit, step by step.
Frame 1: Your first class, minute by minute
